title: Cohomological bounds for scalar extension of a finite-Tor object
statement: Let C be a small site, A and B commutative rings in its coefficient universe, f : A -> B any ring homomorphism, K an object of the standard derived category of constant A-module sheaves, and a <= b integers. Use the Tor test [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude] and normalized scalar extension [lem-sfb-adic-finite-reduction-data]. If K has Tor amplitude [a,b], then the cohomology of extension_f(K) vanishes in every degree q < a or q > b. No Noetherian, constructibility, surjectivity or flatness hypothesis on f is imposed.

source.place: Tags 08G0, 08G1, 06YQ and 06YY; bounded-flat-model argument for the scalar-extension part of parent proof step 2.

proof.text: Apply the coefficient-model flat-model criterion with the supplied ordered Tor interval. Obtain a representative P supported in [a,b], with flat terms and an isomorphism Q(P) -> K.
The bounded-above flat criterion makes P K-flat. The universal computation of scalar extension identifies extension_f(K) with Q(change_f(P)).

Ordinary scalar extension is additive, hence sends the zero terms outside [a,b] to zero. Thus change_f(P) is strictly supported in [a,b]. Its localization has cohomology in that interval. Apply the cohomology functor to the computation and representative isomorphisms to transport this vanishing.

lean.statement:
theorem adicScalarExtension_bound {C : Type w} [SmallCategory C]
    (T : GrothendieckTopology C) {A B : Type w} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    (f : A →+* B) (K : ConstantCompletion.D (constant T A)) (a b : ℤ)
    (hK : HasCoefficientModelTorAmplitude (constant T A) K a b) :
    ∀ q : ℤ, q < a ∨ b < q →
      IsZero ((coefficientModelCohomology (constant T B) q).obj
        ((adicFiniteExtension T f).obj K))
